query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid method that combines high-throughput calorimetric measurements (DSC), in-situ neutron imaging, and advanced CALPHAD simulations (with third‐generation thermodynamic descriptions) will accurately and efficiently determine the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across high‐entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid, single‐phase high‐entropy alloy samples (e.g., transition‐metal based HEAs and related complex concentrated alloys) prepared in as-cast or well-equilibrated conditions.
generation.intervention: Subject the samples to controlled heating protocols using DSC to capture thermal events, while simultaneously performing in-situ neutron imaging during melting. Use the obtained data to calibrate and refine CALPHAD simulations based on third-generation thermodynamic models.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted in inert or vacuum atmospheres, with moderate-to-slow heating rates to minimize thermal lag and ensure equilibrium; temperature spans set to bracket the expected melting transition of each alloy; neutron imaging resolution adjusted to capture liquid-phase homogeneity.
generation.structural_mediator: Local atomic and short-range chemical order in HEAs, which affects the phase transition signatures and can be effectively captured both thermally (by DSC) and structurally (by imaging).
generation.mechanism: During heating, the characteristic endothermic peak (DSC) corresponding to fusion is measured, while the in-situ neutron imaging verifies the liquid phase formation and volume changes. Comparison with CALPHAD simulations incorporating high‐entropy effects allows deconvolution of complex thermodynamic signals into melting temperature, enthalpy/entropy of fusion, and latent volume change.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion properties (melting temperature, enthalpy/entropy of fusion, volume change) will be determined with improved accuracy (error margins expected on the order of 5–10%) compared to traditional single-technique approaches, and the liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will be consistent with third-generation CALPHAD predictions across a broad HEA compositional space.
generation.baseline: Traditional techniques (standalone DSC or indirect thermodynamic estimations) in HEAs often yield larger uncertainties (errors >10–15%) due to compositional complexity and overlapping thermal events.
generation.boundary: This approach may be less applicable in cases with extreme compositional inhomogeneity or where phase separation phenomena dominate the melting behavior; also, limitations in neutron imaging resolution at very high temperatures could impose practical boundaries.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative performance (exact error margins and processing speed) depends on inter-laboratory calibration and may vary with alloy complexity. There is also uncertainty in the extent to which liquid-phase mixing in multi-component systems conforms to the CALPHAD models without further empirical refinement.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of high-entropy alloys covering a wide composition range. Conduct DSC experiments to record fusion characteristics and in-situ neutron imaging to document morphological changes during melting. Separately, perform CALPHAD simulations using third-generation thermodynamic databases. Compare the experimental melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, and volume change data with the simulation outputs.
measurements: DSC thermograms capturing endothermic fusion peaks
Neutron radiographs showing liquid-state mixing and volumetric expansion
Quantitative CALPHAD simulation outputs for fusion properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimental measurements (from DSC and neutron imaging) deviate systematically from the CALPHAD predictions by more than approximately 10% across multiple HEA systems, or if critical thermodynamic parameters cannot be resolved due to overlapping transitions or imaging limitations, then the hybrid approach is falsified.

In-Situ Imaging of Molten High-Entropy Alloys Using Cold Neutrons

Abstract: AbstractReal-time neutron imaging was utilized to produce a movie-like series of radiographs for in-situ observation of the remixing of liquid state immiscibility that occurs in equiatomic CoCrCu with the addition of Ni. A previous neutron imaging study demonstrated that liquid state immiscibility can be observed in-situ for the equiatomic CoCrCu alloy. In this follow-up study, equiatomic buttons of CoCrCu were placed alongside small Ni buttons inside an alumina crucible in a high-temperature vacuum furnace. The mass of the Ni buttons was specifically selected such that when melted in the same crucible as the CoCrCu buttons, the overall composition would become equiatomic CoCrCuNi. Neutron imaging was simultaneously carried out to capture 10 radiographs in 20 °C steps from 1000 °C to 1500 °C and back down to 1000 °C. This, in turn, produced a movie-like series of radiographs that allow for the observation of the buttons melting, the transition from immiscible to miscible as Ni is alloyed into the CoCrCu system, and solidification. Third-Generation Thermodynamic Descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V Binary Systems

Abstract: AbstractThe third-generation thermodynamic descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V binary systems were performed to construct the reliable thermodynamic database for refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) containing Laves phase. The third-generation Gibbs energy expressions of pure Cr and V in both solid and liquid phases were established, from which the thermodynamic properties and thermal vacancy can be well described. The thermodynamic descriptions of Ta-Cr and Ta-V over the whole composition and temperature regions were carried out based on the reviewed phase equilibria and thermodynamic data with the CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagrams) approach. Specifically, the thermodynamic parameters of C14 and C15 Laves phases were evaluated by combining the theoretically computed and experimentally measured thermodynamic properties as well as the semiempirical relations.
